description: Team Phoenix from Dhaka is taking on the "Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots" challenge. Satellite active fire records are currently split across different sensors. We are building an AI-driven "burning activity calendar" that harmonizes decades of data. By unifying these records, our tool empowers scientists and emergency responders to track fire trends, anticipate intense burns, and improve fire response.
summary: Dahan is a web app that combines decades of NASA MODIS and VIIRS active-fire detections into a harmonized fire calendar. It helps emergency responders, forest managers, researchers, and communities explore fire activity for any area through maps, historical comparisons, and downloadable data. A Python and DuckDB pipeline prepares the satellite records, while the browser displays and analyzes the generated data.
details:
What it does and how it works

Dahan (দহন) harmonizes 26 years (November 2000 – Present) of active-fire observations from four NASA satellites (Terra, Aqua, Suomi NPP, NOAA-20, and NOAA-21) into one continuous, seam-free fire calendar for any district, custom polygon, radius buffer, or coordinate on Earth.

When NASA transitioned from MODIS (1,000 m pixel) to VIIRS (375 m pixel), raw detections surged by +400% due to sensor optics, not climate disasters. Dahan eliminates this hardware discrepancy using an Empirical Bayes overlap calibration model with prior shrinkage (pseudo-count of 25) across H3 spatial hexagonal cells (250 km²). Dahan bins all detections by Local Solar Date (UTC+Lon/15∘\text{UTC} + \text{Lon}/15^\circUTC+Lon/15∘) to stop nocturnal fires from splitting across two calendar days, and masks static industrial gas flares and volcanoes (type==0\text{type} == 0type==0).

Instead of heavy centralized databases, our Python and DuckDB data pipeline streams 10 GB of yearly FIRMS GeoParquet into 8,092 compact static H3 partitions. These are distributed via Cloudflare Pages edge CDN, allowing the client browser to decompress and compute harmonized statistics 100% on-the-fly via WebStreams WASM in under 50 milliseconds.

What benefits does it have?

  • Operational Early Warnings: Provides an immediate verdict for the current week—showing whether the season is active, normal, or anomalous, a predictive countdown to the next burning season onset, and crew staging dates.
  • Critical Fire Windows: Pinpoints the exact 2-to-3 calendar weeks that hold 50% and 80% of an area’s entire annual fire load.
  • Dual Scientific Scales: Users can toggle between calibrated Hotspots (VIIRS scale) and sensor-invariant Fire Cell-Days (FCD).
  • Multi-Modal Input: Select any boundary via global search (English and Bangla), draw custom bounding boxes/polygons, apply radius buffers, or upload custom GeoJSON/KML boundary files.
  • Data & Visual Exports: One-click CSV downloads for harmonized weekly/monthly time series, raw-weighted individual hotspot coordinates, and high-resolution PNG charts.
  • 100% Bilingual Accessibility: Complete native localization in English and Bangla with localized numerals, calendar months, and color-vision-deficiency-safe (Cividis and Okabe-Ito) palettes.

What is the intended impact of the project?

Dahan shifts wildfire management from reactive emergency firefighting to proactive seasonal staging. Frontline forest managers, indigenous forest communities (e.g., in Bandarban, Bangladesh), and disaster response agencies can deploy crews, clear fire lines, and position water tankers weeks before peak fires erupt. For climate scientists and policymakers, Dahan provides an unbroken 26-year empirical baseline to assess true climate-driven wildfire trends, evaluate drought/rain risk using NASA POWER precipitation (MERRA-2), and protect global forest carbon sinks.

Tools, coding languages, hardware, and software used

  • Languages: TypeScript, Python 3.12, SQL (DuckDB dialect), HTML5, CSS3.
  • Data Pipeline & Processing: DuckDB (with Spatial & H3 extensions), Apache Arrow, GeoParquet, H3 Hierarchical Spatial Indexing (h3-js, h3-py).
  • Frontend & Visualization: React 19, Vite, MapLibre GL JS, Apache ECharts, Terra Draw, Turf.js.
  • Cloud Infrastructure & Hosting: Cloudflare Pages (Static Edge CDN, KV Cache, Pages Functions / Serverless runtime), GitHub Actions (CI/CD), Docker.
  • APIs & AI: NASA FIRMS Area API, NASA POWER API, Google Gemini Flash API.
  • Open Source License: AGPL-3.0.

How is your project creative?

  1. Zero-Database Client-Side Architecture: Instead of costly server databases, Dahan encodes 26 years of global satellite data into static gzip binary partitions. The browser acts as the database engine via WebStreams WASM, delivering sub-50ms speeds at zero server cost.
  2. Transparent Open-Science Verification: Rather than hiding satellite differences behind a black box, Dahan provides a dedicated Record tab exposing raw MODIS vs. raw VIIRS vs. harmonized records side-by-side, complete with built-in Pettitt change-point test (p>0.05p > 0.05p>0.05) and hold-out cross-validation curves.
  3. Guarded Zero-Hallucination AI: Gemini AI generates automated situation reports, but the server strictly rejects and re-prompts if any number in the generated bulletin does not strictly match the client-computed facts.

Factors our team considered

  • The Naive Concat Trap: Proving that naive merging of MODIS and VIIRS produces an artificial 400% surge at 2012.
  • Low-Bandwidth Reliability: Field rangers in remote areas often have poor connectivity; static edge caching ensures instant loading on mobile browsers.
  • NASA API Quota Protection: A built-in edge cache and 60-degree tile transaction estimation protect NASA’s shared 5,000 transaction/10-min FIRMS budget.
  • Platform Drift Continuity: Adjusting NOAA-20 and NOAA-21 over cross-orbit overlaps to maintain Suomi NPP baseline continuity.
